3. The principal defendant —respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein contested the suit by filing separate written statements refuting all the material allegations as unfolded in the plaint contending in a nutshell that previously the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed a suit for partition in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Nazirpur, Pirojpur being Title Suit No.217 of 1983 against respondent No.2 and others and thereafter the suit was dismissed on contest against which the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.126 of 1986 before the District Judge, Pirojpur and upon hearing the parties the appeal was allowed setting aside the judgement and decree and sending the suit on remand to the trial Court. After remand the suit was decreed, against which the principal defendant-respondent No.2 preferred Title Appeal No.15 of 1990 before the District Judge, who on hearing the parties allowed the appeal and again remanded the suit to the trial Court. At that stage respondent No.1 compromised the suit with respondent No.2, the suit was decreed on the basis of solenama, and as such the present Title Suit No.84 of 2000 is not maintainable. 

 10. It appears from the evidence and materials on record that in the instant suit the plaintiffs sought a declaration that the judgement and decree dated 20.10.2000 in Title Suit No. 217 of 1983 was obtained collusively and fraudulently. The earlier suit was one for partition and was ultimately decreed on the basis of a solenama and the plaintiffs of the instant suit contested the earlier suit and also prayed for saham. We find from the order sheet of earlier partition suit that defendant Nos. 9 to 13 filed an application praying for saham but that application was rejected because the applicants did not sign the application, but the trial Court noted that the earlier suit was decreed giving more than the due share to the defendants, who were party to the solenama. The appellate Court, on the other hand, noted that the solenama decree was passed in the earlier suit on 13.10.1997 and after that defendant Nos. 9 to 13 of that suit, who are the plaintiffs in the present suit filed an application praying for saham which was rejected on 01.03.1998. Their application for saham was filed again and was again rejected on 15.04.1998 and the decree was made final upon receipt of the Advocate Commissioner's report. The appellate Court observed that there was neither any revision filed against the rejection of the application for saham nor any appeal filed against the preliminary or final decree. The appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs could not prove that the earlier suit was decreed without their knowledge and consent. The appellate Court pointed out that P.W. 1 admitted in his cross-examination that they went into possession in accordance with the final decree of Title Suit No. 217 of 1983.
